title: 3-to-8 Decoder
statement: Design a 3-to-8 decoder that converts a 3-bit binary input into an eight-bit one-hot output. Only one output line may be asserted at a time while all others remain low. If the input is out of range, all outputs should remain zero. This module is often used in address decoding and instruction dispatch logic.
behavior: One-hot output: y[i] = 1 when sel equals i, else 0.
All outputs must be driven combinationally.
No use of memories, latches, or sequential blocks.
Purely combinational: outputs must settle after input changes.
Do not depend on initial register values, clocks, or delays.
All outputs must be driven to known 0/1 values for every input case.
constraints: Do not use a behavioral for-loop for the decoder.
hint: Think of the decoder as a binary-to-one-hot converter.
